chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I read to you the bequest of Fatima (peace be upon her)?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, so he brought out a box or a basket, and extracted a letter from it. So he read it: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. This is what Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), bequeathed. I bequeath her seven walled gardens: Al-Awaf, Al-Dallal, Al-Barqa, Al-Maysab, Al-Husna, Al-Safiya, and what belonged to the mother of Ibrahim, to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). So if Ali passes away, then to Al-Hasan. So if Al-Hasan passes away, then to Al-Husayn. So if Al-Husayn passes away, then to the eldest of my children.' Allah was a Witness upon that, and Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad, and Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam; and it was written by Ali ibn Abi Talib.
And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Asim ibn Humayd, similar to it, but did not mention a box or a basket, and she said: 'To the eldest of my children besides your children.'
ai.seo_question: What were the specific properties bequeathed by Fatima (peace be upon her) and who was the ultimate heir?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi details the specific bequest of Fatima bint Muhammad (as) regarding her seven properties, establishing a clear line of succession for inheritance through Ali, Hasan, Husayn, and finally the eldest of her offspring. The inclusion of prominent witnesses like Al-Miqdad, Al-Zubayr, and Ali himself underscores the authenticity and public nature of this will, serving as a key textual evidence for the Ahl al-Bayt's property rights and the principle of inheritance within the Imamate lineage.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Majran, from Aasim Bin Hameed, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> read out to you the bequest of Fatima<sup>asws</sup>?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> brought out a box or a basket, and extracted a letter from it. So he<sup>asws</sup> read: ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Beneficent, the Merciful. This is what has been bequeathed by Fatima<sup>asws</sup> daughter of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. I<sup>asws</sup> hereby bequeath these seven walls (walled gardens) – Al-Dallal, and Al-Barqa, and Al-Maysab, and Al-Husna, and Al-Safiya, and what was for mother of Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>, to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>. So if he<sup>asws</sup> was to pass away, so to Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>. So if Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> was to pass away, so to Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>. So if Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was to pass away, so to the elder from my<sup>asws</sup> children’. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> was a Witness upon that, and Al-Miqdad Bin Al-Aswad, and Al-Zubeyr Bin Al-Awwam; and it was written by Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>’.

And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Aasim Bin Hameed, similar to it, but did not mention a box or a basket, and she<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘To the eldest of my<sup>asws</sup> children besides your<sup>asws</sup> children’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Humayd from abu Basir who has narrated the following:

“Once abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, decided to inform us about an important fact. He (the Imam) said, ‘Do you like if I read the will of Fatimah, ‘Alayha al-Salam, for you?’ I replied, ‘Yes, I like to hear.’ He (the Imam) then took out a box or a basket from which he took out a book (a letter) and read, ‘In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. This is the will of Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. She; bequests all of her seven walls (gardens enclosed by walls), al-‘Awaf, al- Dalal, al-Burqah, al-Maythab, al-Husna’, al-Safiyah and Ma li ’Umm Ibrahim to Ali ibn abu Talib, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. When Ali passes away it then is for al-Hassan, when al-Hassan passes away then it is for al-Husayn and when al-Husayn passes away then it is for the eldest of my children. Allah is witness thereof, al-Miqdad ibn Aswad, al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awam and Ali ibn abu Talib are the scribes.

From the narrator of the previous Hadith from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘ Asem ibn Humayd a similar Hadith is narrated in which he has not mentioned box or basket and has said ... To the eldest of my children other than [not] your children.’
